note: Written before the run. Shape follows check_predictions.episodic_reset_checks: each entry becomes one add(name, verdict, observed, threshold, note, tags) row. MANIFEST.md section 9 states, per row, which fields the checker should read.
brief_corrections: THE SERVING STACK IS NOT BIT-DETERMINISTIC, and the brief's licence to 'demand bit-identity' holds only for a coarse scored statistic, never for rows. In-run proof: the 15 empty-store presentations of 'Next letter: C' at n=1 under episodic_reset are BIT-IDENTICAL requests (n=1 system prompt does not vary across participants; store empty so no block prepended; user message identical). Eleven escaped, four did not -- 4/15 divergence on one identical request.

Cross-arm confirmation. episodic_reset's step() override is provably a no-op on a single-step(), empty-store episode, so every encode()->recall() task issues byte-identical requests under it. Comparing rows by id with server-assigned tool_call_id stripped: semantic_story_recall 199/200 rows differ (scored delta -0.0027), narrative_qa 40/50 (-0.0100), word_recognition 39/50 (+0.0379), craft_task 24/150 (-0.0280), digit_span_reverse 10/190 (0.0000), digit_span_forward 4/190 (0.0000). Under serial_recognition (recall() override that fires only on a >=5 'trial N:' line prompt, which digit span and craft do not have): digit_span_reverse 10/190 and craft_task 12/150, both scored delta 0.0000. Craft is the decisive pair -- 12 differing rows gave 0.0000 and 24 gave -0.0280, same task, same zero mechanism.

THEREFORE the WORKLOG's attribution is wrong: 'episodic_reset's craft (-0.0280) and narrative (-0.0100) moves are genuine effects of its step() rewrite' is false, and so is 'its claim that the six encode()->recall() tasks would be untouched is empirically wrong'. Its structural claim was correct and is reproduced offline against a stub: the requests ARE byte-identical. What failed was its P10 THRESHOLD (a uniform +-0.005), which this stack cannot meet. semantic_story_recall at 199/200 differing rows and -0.0027 is the proof: near-total row divergence, no scored effect.

Second-order consequence: metric_noise.py's bootstrapped floor for craft_task is 0.025, and a provably no-op change moved it -0.0280. The bootstrap resamples the model side of a FIXED set of rows, so it does not capture generation-level run-to-run variation. For craft_task at least, NOISE_FLOOR understates it. P8 registers 0.030 there rather than 0.025.

The pre-committed fix ('pinning the instruction turn') would not have repaired P9: with the instruction turn pinned and the store empty, turn k is still a pure function of the current letter, so the absorbing state survives. AND its premise was false -- the instruction turn is NOT redundant with the system prompt. wm_nback.py:86 uniquely carries 'Update your working memory each turn to track the recent sequence'; the system prompt only says 'Use write_memory and delete_key to maintain the key-value store while doing the original task'.

The failure was NOT 'localised to buffer-period turns': 36 of 50 n=1 rows answered none of the 14 TRIAL turns either. And the per-turn escape is not a hazard over turns, it is letter-conditioned -- C escapes on 11 of 15 empty-store presentations (0.733) against B 1/29, H 1/31, M 1/40 and 0/601 for the other 17 letters -- traceable to the n=1 system prompt's worked example 'A -> A -> B -> C -> C'. A worked example whose letters overlap the stimulus alphabet is a stimulus-contamination hazard for any candidate that reduces context.

inject.load_candidate + apply is NOT IDEMPOTENT and stacking is silent. Loading a candidate file twice in one process gives a second class whose _BaseAgent was resolved at import from bench.core.wm_agent.WorkingMemoryAgent -- which apply() has already rebound to the FIRST candidate class -- so the second subclasses the first and overrides compose. Observed: the control-state block emitted twice in one user message. run_candidate.py:79-80 loads once, so the real pipeline is safe; test scripts and any composed-arm harness must load once.

wm_nback.jsonl does not persist step_log. run_nback_block returns it (wm_nback.py:129) but evaluate() omits it from the row, so the agent's per-turn TEXT on n-back is unrecoverable from a run. 'Did it emit unparseable output?' had to be answered indirectly, via model_parsed_buffer and the contiguity structure. variable_mapping does persist answer_raw.

predictions.name: n=1 nback mechanics repaired -- PRECONDITION

any.reads_as: answered correctly WITHOUT a store, which under this harness is incoherent -- at n=1 the only route to a 1-back judgement is previous_letter in the store. full_context demonstrates the hole is reachable (keys_held 0.80 at 0.9957 accuracy, because its context carried the letter). This leg is the n=1 analogue of P2's letter-share.

predictions.capable_of_varying: episodic_reset moved all three legs hard (13.98->2.06, 0.9943->0.787, 0->36) on real data; random_decay_v2 moved answered to 13.86 and acc to 0.9886. Not inert.
predictions.note: A P1 FAILURE INVALIDATES P2-P7 REGARDLESS OF THEIR VALUES, exactly as episodic_reset's P9 did. At n=1 a single overwritten key suffices and the baseline uses exactly that (previous_letter in 50/50 blocks, keys_held 1.00), so one item in four slots cannot be a capacity failure and nothing measured under a failed P1 can be attributed to the memory module. Mechanism being tested: the ordinals strictly increase, so no two turns are the same request and the near-absorbing state episodic_reset created (empty store -> no block prepended -> turn is a pure function of the letter) is structurally impossible; the empty store is rendered as '(memory is empty)'; and the standing per-turn write directive is present. keys_held at n=1 should return to ~1 from 0.28.

predictions.name: the leak stays closed on n-back, and not by restoring context
quantity: share of n=3 final_kv values containing a bare capital letter, regex (?<![A-Za-z])[A-Z](?![A-Za-z])
predictions.baseline_detail: 4 of 198 values carry a letter; n=1 is 50/50 and n=2 77/77

any.reads_as: the history leak reopened: the store no longer has to carry letter identity, so the answers are coming from somewhere else

predictions.capable_of_varying: letter-share spans 0.0201 (displacement) to 1.0000 (episodic_reset, full_context) across runs; keys_held at n=3 spans 1.06 (full_context) to 4.00 (primacy). Both legs demonstrably move.
predictions.note: This is the row that must survive: it is episodic_reset's single strongest mechanism result. keys_held is REPORTED, NOT THRESHOLDED, and that is a deliberate correction made before the run. A keys_held bar cannot be an anti-restoration test in either direction: it can fail while the mechanism works, because an agent with a leak-free store can legitimately adopt the rolling single-overwritten-key strategy (episodic_reset's own P7 named that branch: 'keys_held falls toward 1 => the agent adopted full_context's rolling single-key strategy'), and it can pass while context is restored, because restored context does not force keys_held down -- episodic_reset held 3.82 WITH the leak closed and primacy held 4.00 WITH the leak open. The anti-restoration work is done by P4 instead: a restored transcript returns variable_mapping to ~12 errors, because the baseline's 0.992 IS the transcript. Also deliberately NOT thresholded on acc_over_answered: a correctly maintained 3-letter store legitimately supports high n=3 accuracy, so an accuracy cap would punish the mechanism working. Report keys_held beside letter-share so the strategy the agent adopted is visible: ~1 means rolling single key, ~4 means positional slots.

predictions.name: no-change control: digit_span_reverse bit-identical, five others within their own measured floors

digit_span_reverse.threshold_note: Point estimate is EXACT equality (0.9666 in all four iteration-2 arms) and a hit should be recorded by _frozen_tag. But the VERDICT-BEARING threshold is NOISE_FLOOR['digit_span_reverse'] = 0.059, not exact equality, because correction 1 shows exact equality is an empirical regularity over four arms and not a structural guarantee: 10 of its 190 rows differed under a provably no-op change. Registering == 0.9666 as the gate would repeat precisely the defect this row exists to correct in episodic_reset's P10 -- a threshold the serving stack cannot guarantee.

predictions.capable_of_varying: digit_span_reverse humanlikeness has moved on real data under mechanisms that do reach it: random_decay -0.2316, random_decay_v2 -0.0701, full_context -0.3986, displacement +0.0138. It is NOT an inert quantity -- it is a quantity this mechanism cannot reach, which is what a no-change control requires. It held at exactly 0.9666 in all four iteration-2 arms.
predictions.why_this_mechanism_cannot_touch_it: wm_digit_span_reverse builds a fresh agent per trial (wm_digit_span_reverse.py:110) and goes encode() -> recall(). encode() calls step() exactly once, so _episode_turn_index() == 1 and no control-state block is prepended; recall() is not overridden. Verified offline against a stub: the encode() tool-call request stream and the recall() prompt are BYTE-IDENTICAL to baseline's.
predictions.structural_claim: The same argument applies to all six legs -- the requests are byte-identical for every one of them. digit_span_reverse is the one whose scored statistic is coarse enough that exact equality is the expected outcome (W_1 over 10 model pseudo-participants; it held at exactly 0.9666 in 4/4 arms despite 10-42 of its 190 rows differing in each), which is why it carries expected_exact and the FROZEN tag -- but its verdict threshold is still its noise floor, for the reason in its threshold_note.
predictions.threshold_derivation: Each non-exact leg is its own NOISE_FLOOR value, except craft_task, raised from 0.025 to 0.030, and semantic_story_recall, tightened from 0.030 (FLOOR) to 0.015. Reasons: a provably no-op change (episodic_reset) moved craft -0.0280, past its bootstrapped floor of 0.025, so the bootstrap understates generation-level run-to-run variation there; whereas story recall stayed inside 0.006 in all four iteration-2 arms despite 199/200 rows differing, so 0.015 is achievable and 0.030 would be slack.
predictions.note: This row is the explicit correction to episodic_reset's P10, which registered a uniform +-0.005 on all six and FAILED on a threshold the serving stack cannot meet, not on a mechanism. See brief_corrections 1-4. Any nonzero movement on these five legs is serving nondeterminism and must not be narrated as a mechanism effect; the row exists so that it is recorded as nondeterminism rather than attributed.

offline_verification.verify_interface: PASS -- WorkingMemoryAgent rebound in 8 modules, SummarizerAgent 8, CONDITION_PROMPTS/TOOLS/MAX_KEYS in their defining modules; encode/recall round trip returns the expected shapes; capacity enforced at 4.
offline_verification.structural_context_test: PASS, 0 failures. Drove the REAL wm_nback.run_nback_block at n=1, 2, 3 and the REAL variable_mapping loop against a recording stub LLM. Asserted: the first generate_with_tools call of EVERY step() receives exactly 2 messages (system + user), at every level, INCLUDING all buffer-period turns; no request anywhere (including inside the tool-dispatch loop) contains more than one 'Next letter:'; step 1 carries no control-state block and still carries the task's own instruction text; every later step carries the block and renders the store; turn ordinals strictly increasing and unique; on variable_mapping the store header is never duplicated on the question turn and no turn shows more than its own TURNS_PER_QUESTION=2 statements.
offline_verification.first_letter_turn: The turn episodic_reset failed on now reads: '[ongoing episode] / Turn 2 of this episode. Stimulus presentations so far: 1. / You have no transcript of earlier turns: the key-value store is your only record of them. Update it each turn to track what you will need later. / Your working memory currently contains: / (memory is empty) / / Next letter: R'. The empty store is explicit and the turn is distinguishable from every other turn, so the near-absorbing state is structurally impossible.
offline_verification.no_op_test: PASS -- encode() -> recall() request stream BYTE-IDENTICAL between baseline and episodic_reset_v2 (tool-call request list and the recall() prompt both).
offline_verification.what_is_NOT_verified: Behaviour. Nothing here tests what the frozen LLM will actually do -- whether it now writes on turn 1 and answers from the store is PREDICTED (P1), not measured. No model was run. The verification covers the STRUCTURE of the context only.

composition.target: episodic_reset_v2 o primacy, as a third arm
composition.runtime_error_note: episodic_reset.step() raised RuntimeError when len(store) > _capacity(). This candidate does NOT. It was dead under the baseline's write_key (which refuses rather than overflows), but under a composed overflow rule a transient overflow would turn a degraded row into a hard job crash, and the invariant belongs to write_key. Safe to compose in that respect.
composition.surfaces_disjoint: This candidate overrides step() and nothing else. WorkingMemory is not subclassed; write_key, the overflow policy and the eviction order are untouched (primacy owns them); recall(), encode(), TOOLS, CONDITION_PROMPTS, WM_SYSTEM_PROMPTS, _tool_call_cap() and MAX_KEYS are untouched.
composition.interaction_the_composed_arm_must_respec: NOT ADDITIVE. Under the baseline step() the store was never rendered into a turn, so eviction order was unobservable during a step()-driven task. Under this candidate to_recall_text() is on the prompt path every turn, so primacy's eviction -- both WHICH key dies and the ORDER survivors are listed in -- becomes part of the agent's context on nback and variable_mapping. Some of the composed effect may come from the agent reacting to a visibly changed store rather than from the eviction rule. Worth its own prediction row in the composed arm.
composition.attribute_contract: self._step_log and self._tool_interactions are READ, never written, before super().step(). A composed candidate that also overrides step() must call super().step() exactly once per turn and must not pre-increment _tool_interactions, or the reported presentation ordinal will be wrong.
composition.reset_placement: reset_messages() must stay at the turn boundary, never inside the tool-dispatch loop: clearing mid-loop leaves a 'tool' message with no preceding assistant 'tool_calls' and the request is rejected.
composition.single_load: The composed arm must be ONE candidate file, loaded once. See brief_corrections 7: load_candidate + apply is not idempotent and stacking is silent.
